advices.diagnosis: The class has a very high method count (NOM=26) and accumulated cyclomatic complexity (WMC=56), while its cohesion is poor (LCOM4=5), which together flag a classic god‑class smell. The feature‑envy candidate indicates that some behavior (order‑related logic) is more interested in the Order domain object than its own state. These metrics suggest the class is doing too many unrelated responsibilities and should be broken up.

suggestions.title: Extract focused service classes from OrderService
suggestions.sketch:
Create four new classes in the application layer:
- OrderLifecycleService: methods place, fetch, cancel, close, order_count, orders_for, open_orders, line_count, revenue, tier_summary.
- PricingService: methods set_discount, discount_for, bulk_discount, set_tax_rate, apply_tax, total_for, policy_rate, is_priced.
- AuditService: methods log, history, last_entry, audit_size, clear_audit.
- NotificationService: methods notify, sent_count, reset_sent.
Inject these collaborators into a slimmed OrderService façade that only coordinates calls. Adjust imports so the new services still depend on domain classes (Customer, Order, etc.) but remain within the application layer.

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class introduces new public APIs; existing code that directly uses OrderService methods will need to be updated to use the façade or the new services. Care must be taken to preserve transaction boundaries and side‑effects (e.g., audit logging and notification counters) during the refactor. Unit tests should be updated to reflect the new composition, and integration tests must verify that behavior remains unchanged.
